Article 1.2: Choosing Your Account: Standard vs Express, OG vs MAX

Warren's summary

When purchasing an account, you choose three things: Account Type (Standard or Express), Account Style (OG or MAX), and Account Size ($25,000 to $250,000). Standard accounts require longer evaluation periods (7 days for OG or 5 winning days for MAX) with a 40% consistency rule, while Express accounts have shorter evaluation periods (4 days for OG or 2 days for MAX) with lower consistency requirements (25% for OG or 50% for MAX). OG accounts are no longer sold but existing OG accounts keep their rules; they include an exhibition stage that builds a buffer before funding, while MAX accounts go straight to funded with the buffer built inside. Both account types charge a $120 activation fee, which may be waived in promotions.

The Three Selection Dimensions

When purchasing an account, traders select three things:

Account Type: Standard or Express
Account Style: OG or MAX
Account Size: $25,000 to $250,000
Account Type: Standard vs Express
Feature	Standard	Express
Minimum trading days (eval)	OG Standard: 7 days / Standard MAX: 5 winning days	OG Express: 4 days / Express MAX: 2 days
Consistency rule (eval)	40%	25% (OG) / 50% (MAX)
Evaluation drawdown type	Realized Trailing (OG) / EOD (MAX)	Realized Trailing
Daily Loss Limit in eval	None (OG) / Soft breach (MAX)	None
Best use case	Traders who prefer longer windows	Traders who want fastest path to funding
Account Style: OG vs MAX

OG accounts are no longer sold. Existing OG accounts keep their rules.

Feature	OG	MAX
Exhibition stage	YES: builds buffer before funding	NO: goes straight to funded
Buffer built in	Exhibition account	Funded account
Drawdown in funded (sim)	Static +$100 (locks after buffer built)	EOD (Standard) or Unrealized Trailing (Express)
Funded consistency rule	40% (sim) / None (live)	40% Standard / 25% Express MAX (sim)
Contract limit during eval	Per account scaling plan max	Per account scaling plan max
Activation fee	$120 (may be waived in promotions)	$120 (may be waived in promotions)
IMPORTANT: 'OG' stands for the original FFN account structure: evaluation → exhibition → funded. 'MAX' is a newer structure: evaluation → funded directly (buffer built inside the funded account).
